desc: The Puffs went to their first show of the year! Here is my full bath routine for a horse show. When the Puffs are shining & feeling their best, they perform their best!  1) Unbraid  2) Tidy up the bridle path, feather undercut, and tail undercut with Wahl KMC+ clipper.  3) Gentle Shampoo on the face, purple down the blaze and on the mustache! I use Cowboy Magic Yellow Out.  4) Head & Shoulders on the mane & body. Scrub, scrub, scrub with washing gloves!  5) Conditioner on everything, then rinse.  6) Throw a fleece on to keep her warm and drying while I do the feather & tail. Feather first, tail last.  7) Head & Shoulders on the feather, then purple or blue, then conditioner, and rinse. Comb out any build up.  8) Dunk the tail in a bucket of Head & Shoulders and warm water. Scrub and soak. Condition & Rinse.  9) Apply Cowboy Magic Detangler & Shine to wet mane, tail, and feather. Brush out when more dry.  10) Shoulder Gaurd to protect the hair (she can’t wear a full slinky because she hates it and rubs), show sheet, braid and vetwrap the tail in one huge braid for travel, and slide into a bag.  Washing before the show helps me be able to focus on settling the horses in once we arrive. I do touch up grooming at the show and it’s so much easier!  #equestrian #grooming #horselover #gypsyvanner #horse

desc: Soy Beans Ep.2 Tofu Tofu Recipe Ingredients * Dried Soybeans: 500g (Soak in 2.5x the weight of dry beans) * Water: 2000g (4x the weight of dry beans) * Gansu (Nigari) : 20~25g (4~5% of the dry soy bean weight) Instructions 1. Soak dried soybeans and water in a 1:2.5 ratio for 10 hours 2. Blend 3. Strain -> Solid (biji) + Liquid (soy milk) 4. Boil the soy milk (to remove trypsin inhibitors, eliminate the raw beany taste, and ensure proper protein coagulation) 5. When it reaches 80~85°C, turn off the heat and add gansu 6. Stir and let it sit for 10 minutes 7. Prepare a mold and cheesecloth, then pour tofu into it 8. Press with a heavy weight for 10 minutes to finish the tofu Gansu (Nigari) * What is gansu : A liquid rich in minerals such as calcium and sulfates * Where does it comes from: It is collected during the sea salt production process, where minerals like calcium and sulfates are separated over 5 years

desc: BROWN BUTTER DUBAI CHOCOLATE CHIP COOKIES Can you even 🥹 Recipe below OR go to my website through the link in my bio 🤎 #Recipe Details (makes 16-18 cookies): Brown Butter Chocolate Chip Cookies: - 1 cup + 2 tbsp (258g) salted butter - 1 cup (230g) brown sugar  - 1/2 cup (110g) granulated sugar  - 2 eggs, at room temp - 2 tbsp (30ml) heavy cream, room temp (sub: milk of choice) - 2 tsp (8g) vanilla extract - 2 3/4 cups (350g) all-purpose flour @Bob’s Red Mill  - 1 tsp (6g) baking soda - 1 tsp (4g) baking powder - 1/4 tsp (2g) salt - 1 1/2 cups (300g) chocolate chips of choice (I used semi-sweet) @Nestle Toll House  Filling: - 1 cup (90g) kataifi (shredded phyllo dough) - 3/4 cup (200g) pistachio butter or cream  - 1 tbsp (14g) salted butter, for toasting kataifi Instructions: Start by browning the butter. Add the butter to a saucepan over medium-high heat. Allow to melt and slightly brown (~5 minutes). Remove from the heat and immediately pour into a large bowl. Allow to cool slightly. In a medium bowl whisk together the flour, baking soda, and baking powder. Set aside. Once the brown butter has cooled, add both sugars and whisk. Add in the eggs and whisk until well combined and lighter in color. Then, add the heavy cream and vanilla. Whisk to combine. Add the dry ingredients to the wet, and gently fold until fully incorporated. Fold in the chocolate chips. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and place in the fridge to chill for at least 1-2 hours (ideally 2-4 hours) or up to 24 hours. I let mine sit in the fridge overnight! Prepare the filling. In a large pan over medium heat, melt the 1 tbsp of butter and add the shredded kataifi. Toast the kataifi until golden and crispy, stirring frequently. Transfer to a bowl and let cool. Once cooled, add the pistachio butter and mix until well combined.  Line a baking sheet with parchment or wax paper. Scoop and portion out the filling into 2 tsp sized balls, placing onto the baking sheet. Chill in the fridge or freezer for at least 1 hour. Once ready to bake, preheat the oven to 375F. Line 2 baking sheets with parchment paper. Remove the dough from the fridge and allow to sit at room temperature for 20-25 minutes to make it easier to scoop. If it needs longer, let it sit longer! Use a large cookie scoop (3 tbsp) to scoop (pack the dough into the scoop with your hands) the dough out. Flatten each ball with your hands. Place the filling portions into the center and shape the dough around it to form cookie balls, adding a little more dough if needed to ensure the filling is completely enclosed.  Place the cookie dough balls on the prepared baking sheets, spacing at least 2” apart.  Bake at 375F for 14-16 minutes, until lightly golden and the edges are set. Remove the cookies from the oven and immediately shape them with a bowl or round cookie cutter if desired. Let cool on the baking sheet for 5 minutes before transferring to a wire cooling rack. Serve warm with a sprinkle of flaky sea salt and milk, if desired. Enjoy! #brownbutter #dubai #chocolatechip #cookies #brownbutterchocolatechipcookies #brownbutterchocolatechipcookierecipe #chocolatechipcookies #chocolatechipcookierecipe #softcookies #gooeycookies #thebestbrownbutterchocolatechipcookies #dubaichocolate #dubaichocolatebar #dubaichocolatechipcookies #dubaichocolatechipcookierecipe #dubaicookies #dubaicookierecipe #chocolate #pistachio #pistachiobutter #pistachiocream #kataifi #baking #dessert @From Our Place @Earlywood

desc: Most recycled polyester is made from PET plastic, often old plastic bottles, that gets shredded, melted down, and spun into synthetic fibers. Then it gets turned into leggings, sports bras, workout tops, underwear, pajamas, and clothes we wear directly on our skin for hours. The problem is that “recycled” does not mean non-toxic. It does not mean natural. It does not mean breathable. It does not mean something I want sitting on my skin while I’m sweating. It is still synthetic. It is still plastic-based. It can still shed microplastics. It can still be treated with dyes, finishes, stretch chemicals, odor-control coatings, and performance additives. desc: Homemade American Bread 🇺🇸🍞 Disclaimer: this is a funny video- nothing more, nothing less. I did not eat this bread. This is a demonstration of the industrial processing steps used in mass-produced bread in the United States. This video is for entertainment and educational purposes only- do not replicate these steps at home. This video does not claim that eating bread will directly harm you. It's meant to shed light on how highly processed most commercial bread has become- especially when mass-produced for consistency, cost-cutting, and shelf stability. This isn't about Wonder Bread specifically- it's a composite of common industry practices- stripping the grain of its nutrients then "enriching" it with synthetic vitamins, bleaching flour with chlorine gas, and loading it with dough conditioners, preservatives, and additives that are banned in dozens of countries but still perfectly legal in the US. This video is describing the general process in a way that can be done on a small scale at home, BUT is not mirroring the exact process- it's optimized to make a watchable video- for example, real industrial mills process thousands of pounds of grain per hour with automated systems, meter in additives at precise levels, and bake at scale… things that are not shown in the video. Potassium bromate btw can be classified as a processing aid so it might not even be listed on the label ‼️ “Generally recognized as safe" might mean it’s not gonna drop you on the spot, but doesn’t mean it’s optimal for you. At the end of the day, eat what you want- but be informed about what you're actually eating.
